name: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF): India's 2027 Blending Mandate
scope: India's SAF blending roadmap for international flights (1% 2027, 2% 2028, 5% 2030), the draft National SAF Policy, refinery co-processing and ethanol-to-jet projects, and listed-company exposure (PSU refiners, Praj and adjacent names).

summary.one_line: India's 2027 SAF target looks deliverable by PSU refiners co-processing used cooking oil, but the draft policy has no prices yet; listed exposure is mainly PSU large caps plus Praj, which has fallen hard, and no small cap has a confirmed SAF contract.
key_points: The 17 April 2026 amendment to the ATF Control Order brought co-processed SAF (IS 1571) and SAF blended to IS 17081 into the ATF definition. The 1% (2027), 2% (2028) and 5% (2030) international-flight targets were described as indicative (S1).

A draft National SAF Policy circulated in early November 2026 would make blending mandatory for international flights from 2027. Only SAF made in India would qualify, and airlines would have to uplift at least 90% of their sector fuel in India. Reports of the 2040 target differ: 40% (S2) versus 20% (S4).

Corn, soybeans and palm oil would be barred as feedstocks, while cane molasses, cane syrup and surplus sugar remain eligible for alcohol-to-jet. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas would set fixed procurement prices, but the draft gives no price levels or margins (S3).

S&P Global and the SAF Association estimate demand at about 46,000 t in 2027 and 250,000 t in 2030. Against this, four ISCC-CORSIA certified co-processing sites hold 106,500 t/yr of capacity: BPCL Mumbai 61,000 t, IOC Panipat 30,000 t, HPCL Visakh 10,000 t and MRPL 5,500 t. The report says that covers 2027-28 but not 2030 (S5).

The capex pipeline beyond co-processing includes IOC's 50:50 joint venture with M11 Energy Transition: a 100 KTPA HEFA plant at Paradip costing Rs 1,063.6 cr (±30%), still awaiting NITI Aayog and DIPAM approval (S7, S8). It also includes IOC's LanzaJet alcohol-to-jet plant at Panipat, planned for 2027-28 (S10), and NTPC's 1,800 tpa ethanol-to-jet plant, built by GPS Renewables, with its contract scope running to March 2029 (S15).

Praj got a detailed-engineering order for an ethanol-to-SAF plant from an international customer in Q1 FY27 but disclosed no value (S16). Its backlog was Rs 4,455 cr at Q2 FY27 (S18). The stock hit a 52-week low of Rs 241.35 on 30 Oct 2026, against a 52-week high of Rs 427.75 (S19, S20).

The draft policy estimates SAF costs 2-3x conventional jet fuel (S4). Platts assessed SAF at about $2,435/t FOB Straits at end-H1 2026 (S5). Who pays the premium (refiners, airlines or passengers) is not yet specified (S2).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Technology and EPC suppliers win orders whether or not SAF is profitable for producers. Praj has an international ethanol-to-SAF engineering order (S16). GPS Renewables (unlisted), Lummus and Xytel are on NTPC's ethanol-to-jet plant (S15).

Refiners with certified co-processing (BPCL Mumbai, IOC Panipat, HPCL Visakh, MRPL) can meet early volumes with little capex. BPCL's revamp needs no new dedicated SAF unit (S13), and co-processing capacity covers 2027-28 demand (S5).
Sugar and distillery companies benefit at the margin because molasses, cane syrup and surplus sugar stay eligible for alcohol-to-jet (S3). No listed sugar company has a disclosed SAF contract (S21).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: If the fixed-price or subsidy mechanism is late or under-funded, the cost premium falls on PSU refiners and airlines. The draft does not say how costs will be shared (S2, S3).

UCO supply is tight. India could generate 1.8-2.6 Mt/yr of UCO, but only a fraction is collected through traceable chains (S5). Feedstock imports are under consideration (S6), and biodiesel makers compete for the same oil (S2).
The 2030 target needs standalone HEFA and ATJ plants to come online in 2028-30 (S5). Most of these still await approvals or are years from commissioning (S7, S10, S15).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Final approval of the National SAF Policy, including the 2040 target (20% or 40%), procurement prices, and support of up to 30% of capex for new plants (S3, S4).
Whether BPCL's Mumbai kerosene hydrotreater revamp is commissioned by end-2026 (S13), and whether HPCL produces about 10,000 t/yr at Visakh from January 2027 (S11).
Q3 FY27 results from Praj (order intake, any SAF order values) and from the oil marketing companies (S18).

sections.title: What SAF is and which pathways matter for India

blocks.text: Sustainable aviation fuel is a drop-in jet fuel made from non-fossil feedstocks. In April 2026 India widened the definition of ATF to include SAF co-processed with ATF in refineries (IS 1571) and SAF blended with ATF to IS 17081 (S1). Three routes matter. The first is co-processing used cooking oil in existing hydrocrackers or hydrotreaters, typically at up to 5% of feed (S12, S13). The second is standalone HEFA plants, such as IOC-M11 at Paradip (S7). The third is alcohol-to-jet (ATJ), which converts ethanol to jet fuel; examples are IOC-LanzaJet at Panipat and NTPC at Pudimadaka (S10, S15). Raw ethanol cannot be blended into jet fuel; it must first be converted by ATJ (S4).

blocks.text: India's sugarcane and molasses ethanol capacity already supplies 1.5 billion litres to the E20 petrol programme. Under ICAO default values, sugarcane ATJ can cut greenhouse gases by up to 73% versus Jet-A1. However, the EU's ReFuelEU rules exclude sugarcane ethanol, so exports to Europe would need second-generation feedstock (S5).

sections.title: Mandate, pricing model and supply build-out

subsections.title: Mandate timeline, pricing and the CORSIA link

blocks.caption: Policy milestones
rows: ATF Control Order amended to include SAF; indicative targets of 1% (2027), 2% (2028), 5% (2030) for international flights
Draft National SAF Policy circulated by the Ministry of Civil Aviation: mandatory from 2027, 1% rising to 5% in phase 1 (2027-30), only Indian-made SAF qualifies, at least 90% fuel uplift in India
Longer-term target reported as 40% by 2040 (S2), or 20% by 2040 with 7.5% possible by 2035 (S3, S4); a 3% step in 2029 is also reported (S4)
Pricing: MoPNG would set fixed procurement prices every year or six months, by technology; OMCs could be compensated for the gap to market prices; support of up to 30% of capex for new plants

blocks.text: The targets align with CORSIA's mandatory phase, which India joins next year. CORSIA does not itself mandate SAF; airlines can use eligible SAF to reduce their offsetting obligations (S4). The draft also proposes a DGCA-run National SAF Registry and a National Council on SAF (S2). The draft expects 8-10 Mt/yr of SAF output by 2040, needing about $70-85 bn of investment (S3).

S&P Global and the SAF Association put mandated demand at about 46,000 t in 2027 and about 250,000 t in 2030. Certified co-processing capacity is 106,500 t/yr, which the report says covers 2027 and 2028; 2030 needs greenfield HEFA and ATJ plants online between 2028 and 2030 (S5). A second estimate is much higher. PSU Watch, reporting the draft policy, puts ATF demand at 14.2 Mt by 2030, which would mean about 710,000 t of SAF at 5% (S2). That appears to apply 5% to all ATF, not just international uplift, but the sources do not reconcile the two figures.

subsections.title: Refiners: volumes are small, the risk is margins

blocks.text: For the PSU refiners, SAF volumes are very small next to their fuel businesses. Total certified co-processing capacity across BPCL, IOC, HPCL and MRPL is 106,500 t/yr (S5). Demand in 2027 is about 46,000 t (S5), while India uses roughly 8.2 Mt of ATF a year (S2). The earnings question is the price gap. Platts assessed SAF at about $2,435/t at end-H1 2026 (S5), and the draft policy puts SAF at 2-3x jet fuel (S4). Until procurement prices and the OMC gap-compensation mechanism are set, refiners carry the risk of selling blended fuel below cost (S3). The largest committed capex is IOC's Paradip JV, at about Rs 1,063.6 cr (S7).

This edition found no disclosure of SAF revenue or margin from any refiner. With volumes this small, SAF is unlikely to move refiner earnings in 2027 either way; it matters mainly as a policy and capex-allocation signal.

subsections.title: Praj Industries and the technology/EPC layer

blocks.text: Praj is the only listed pure technology supplier with SAF engineering work. In Q1 FY27 it won a detailed-engineering order for an ethanol-to-SAF plant from an international customer, after doing basic engineering for the same customer. Management also cited ICAO's approval of the sugarcane-to-jet pathway (S16). Praj has worked with IndianOil since 2021, starting with an agreement to form a 50:50 biofuels JV, followed by a 6 July 2023 term sheet covering SAF, ethanol, CBG, biodiesel and bio-bitumen (S24). It also signed an MoU with IATA and ISMA in 2025 to develop India-specific SAF carbon-intensity certification (S23). Praj does not disclose how much of its backlog is SAF. The bioenergy segment made up 69% of Q2 FY27 revenue, and the total backlog was Rs 4,455 cr (S18).

subsections.title: Other names checked: NTPC, EIL, sugar and biodiesel small caps

items: NTPC passes the evidence bar as a SAF project owner: it awarded the EPC contract for a 1,800 tpa ethanol-to-jet plant (S15). The EPC contractor, GPS Renewables, is unlisted (S15).
Engineers India (EIL) designed a bio-ATF plant at MRPL and in 2025 targeted commercial launch by end-2026 (S25). No 2026 update was found.
Balrampur Chini, a mid cap, gains only indirectly from molasses eligibility for ATJ; no SAF contract is disclosed (S3, S21).

Small caps: Kotyark Industries and Rajputana Biodiesel are listed UCO-based biodiesel makers (S22). This edition found no SAF supply contract for either; their link is indirect, through competition for UCO and OMC biodiesel tenders (S2, S22). IOC's Paradip partner, M11 Energy Transition, is a private company (S7).

blocks.text: Market-cap coverage gap: no small cap with a confirmed SAF contract was found. Exposure is concentrated in PSU large caps, NTPC and one mid-cap technology supplier, Praj.

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

blocks.text: Elara Securities' August 2026 note on Praj kept a negative stance. It cited project delays, weak operating leverage and investment in GenX, and said newer businesses are too nascent to offset core weakness, with benefits possibly from H2FY27. Elara forecasts FY27 revenue of Rs 3,430 cr at an 8.4% EBITDA margin (S17). MarketsMojo linked the October sell-off to flat quarterly results and reliance on non-operating income (S20). Coverage that uses the label 'SAF stocks' is mostly retail commentary. One piece, for example, groups Praj, Godavari Biorefineries and Balrampur Chini but says the sugar names' exposure is indirect (S21).

blocks.text: As of 21 Oct 2026, Praj's one-year return was -22.4% (S19). The 30 Oct close of Rs 241.35 was about 44% below the 52-week high of Rs 427.75 (S19, S20). This edition could not independently confirm the brief's figure of a ~38% fall over six months, but the cited prices are consistent with a de-rating of that size. The market is not treating Praj as a SAF winner; SAF is too early and too small in its order book to offset weak core margins (S17, S18).

companies.name: Indian Oil Corporation
companies.role: Panipat refinery is ISCC CORSIA certified for UCO co-processing (S10), with 30,000 t/yr capacity (S5). It is also planning a LanzaJet alcohol-to-jet plant at Panipat for 2027-28 (S10), and its board approved a 50:50 JV with M11 Energy Transition for a 100 KTPA HEFA plant at Paradip (S7, S8).
companies.impact: Has the largest SAF capex commitment among refiners: Rs 1,063.6 cr ±30% for Paradip, still subject to NITI Aayog/DIPAM approval (S7). Earnings exposure depends on the still-unpriced procurement mechanism (S3).

companies.name: Bharat Petroleum Corporation
companies.role: Mumbai refinery received ISCC CORSIA certification for SAF in June 2026 (S14). It is revamping a 4,000 t/day kerosene hydrotreater with a Topsoe licence to co-process 5% UCO, with commissioning targeted by end-2026 (S13).
companies.impact: Holds the largest certified co-processing capacity, 61,000 t/yr, more than India's estimated 2027 demand of ~46,000 t (S5). It needs little new capex, but carries cost-gap risk until prices are fixed (S3).

companies.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation
companies.role: Commissioned a UCO co-processing demonstration plant at Visakh in January 2026 and expects ~10,000 t/yr from January 2027, subject to CORSIA certification (S11). It is also building a 7.4 KTPA commercial unit on its in-house HP-TriJet technology (S12).
companies.impact: Volumes are small next to its refining business; the in-house technology gives it an option on standalone HEFA (S12).

companies.name: Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals
companies.role: Holds 5,500 t/yr of certified co-processing capacity (S5). In May 2026 it tendered for 35,000 t of Indian UCO for delivery from 1 Sep 2026 to 31 Aug 2027 (S6, S9).
companies.impact: Has the smallest certified capacity of the four; its UCO procurement is an early test of feedstock availability and pricing (S5, S6).

companies.name: Praj Industries
companies.role: Supplies ethanol-to-SAF technology and engineering; won a detailed-engineering order from an international customer in Q1 FY27 (S16). Has a long-standing biofuels partnership with IndianOil that covers SAF (S24) and an MoU with IATA and ISMA on SAF certification (S23).
companies.impact: Benefits from ATJ capex whether or not SAF is profitable for producers, but SAF's share of the Rs 4,455 cr backlog is not disclosed (S18). The stock was at a 52-week low of Rs 241.35 on 30 Oct 2026 (S20).

companies.name: NTPC
companies.role: Awarded the EPC contract for a 1,800 tpa ethanol-to-jet SAF plant at NTPC Green Energy's Pudimadaka hub to GPS Renewables, with a Lummus licence (S15).
companies.impact: A pilot-scale project, immaterial to NTPC's earnings; its value is as a demonstration of the e-ethanol-to-jet route, with scope running to March 2029 (S15).

companies.name: Engineers India
companies.role: Designed a bio-ATF plant at MRPL using technology developed with CSIR-IIP; in 2025 it targeted commercial launch by end-2026 (S25).
companies.impact: Has an engineering-services option on SAF plant build-out; no 2026 status update was found (S25).

companies.name: Balrampur Chini Mills
companies.role: Integrated sugar and distillery producer with 1,050 KLPD of distillery capacity (S21). Molasses and cane syrup remain eligible ATJ feedstocks under the draft policy (S3).
companies.impact: Exposure is indirect; no SAF or ATJ contract is disclosed (S21).

companies.name: Kotyark Industries
companies.role: Small-cap listed biodiesel maker that uses UCO among its feedstocks; one of three listed biodiesel companies (S22).
companies.impact: Adjacency only: it competes for UCO with SAF co-processing (S2), and no SAF contract was found. OMC biodiesel tenders are the nearer driver (S22).

method: First edition, researched on 2026-11-17 using web search and direct page fetches. Several primary pages blocked fetching (PIB, BPCL, S&P Global); their facts were taken only from search-result text and are cited to the original URLs. Two company PDFs (Praj Q1 FY27 presentation and transcript) could not be parsed, so Praj figures come from Elara via DSIJ, Indian Chemical News and an earnings-call summary. Where sources conflict, both figures are shown: the 2040 target (20% vs 40%), 2030 SAF demand (250 kt vs 710 kt) and the cost multiple (the draft policy says 2-3x; the brief's 3-5x was not confirmed). The S23 date is approximate to the month (June 2025, from the file path). S8's capacity figure comes from its headline. The bse field for Kotyark is null because it could not be confirmed. No ratings or price targets are given; broker views are attributed by name. numbers.json was not present in the folder.
